## What Is a VF Corporation Internship?


VF Corporation's U.S. Summer Internship Program is a 12-week, hybrid experience that places students across iconic brands including The North Face, Vans, Timberland, JanSport, and Smartwool. Interns work on meaningful projects, participate in a collaborative group project with an internal consulting focus, and present at an end-of-program showcase. Glassdoor reports 100% positive interview experience from intern candidates with an average time-to-hire of just 21 days. The program is a legitimate pathway into one of the world's largest apparel companies, with 50% off VF brands and exposure to senior leadership as standard perks.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


VF Corporation sets clear eligibility requirements for its summer internship program.


• **Class year:** Junior or senior enrolled in a US 4-year university, ideally graduating May 2026–June 2027


• **Degree:** Marketing, Business, Communications, International Studies, or related field (varies by track)


• **Work authorization:** US Citizen, US Permanent Resident, or US Student Visa accepted — more inclusive than many peers


• **In-person:** Must be able to work in-person for the full 12-week program (hybrid, 3 in-office days)


• **Cover letter:** Required — explain why you are interested and how the role aligns with your career aspirations


• **Experience:** No prior experience required, though retail or brand marketing background is preferred for some roles


### Does VF Corporation Have a GPA Cutoff for Interns?


No. VF publishes no GPA requirement or preference in any of the intern job descriptions reviewed for this guide. The focus is on class year, relevant coursework or degree field, and organizational and communication skills. Students should not self-select out based on GPA — VF screens for brand passion, storytelling ability, and collaborative mindset rather than a numeric threshold.

## What Is the VF Corporation Application and Interview Process Like?


VF Corporation uses Workday for all applications. The interview process is straightforward and fast.


1. **Go to the Workday board** at vfc.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/vfc_careers — this is the source of truth, not brand websites.


2. **Browse by area of interest** and indicate your top choices in the application questionnaire.


3. **Submit your resume AND cover letter** explaining why you are interested and how the role aligns with your career aspirations.


4. **Phone screen with HR** — initial fit and motivation conversation.


5. **Zoom interview with hiring manager** — role-specific questions about brand knowledge and relevant experience.


6. **Offer** — average time from application to offer is approximately 21 days.


Glassdoor rates VF's intern interview process at 2.6/5 difficulty with 100% positive experience. One candidate reports: "First I talked with HR through phone interview. Then I talked with hiring manager over Zoom. Very simple and straightforward."

## How Do You Stand Out at VF Corporation?


First, write the cover letter VF actually asks for — not a generic one. Name the specific brand, reference a recent campaign or product launch (like The North Face's latest outdoor collection or Vans' cultural collaborations), and explain what you would bring to that team. Second, pick your brand and own it. VF asks you to rank your preferred roles in the application questionnaire, so arrive knowing whether you want marketing at Timberland, product development at Vans, or events at Altra. Third, know that VF hires across functions beyond just marketing. Supply chain, finance, and product development tracks exist and see less competition from the creative-focused applicant pool.

## FAQ


### Are VF Corporation internship applications open for summer 2027?


No. The summer 2026 intern postings closed on January 7, 2026, and the summer 2027 cycle has not opened yet. Based on the previous cycle, applications are expected to appear on VF's Workday board in mid-to-late November 2026 and close around early January 2027.


### How long is the VF Corporation internship?


Twelve weeks, running from May through August. Most positions are full-time at 40 hours per week, though some roles are part-time at 24 hours per week. The program operates on a hybrid schedule with three in-office days at one of VF's four US hubs.


### How much do VF Corporation interns get paid?


VF's published hiring range is $18.00 to $22.50 per hour. This rate appeared on every summer 2026 intern posting regardless of brand or location. VF also mentions eligibility for additional incentive compensation, though details are shared during the interview process.


### Where are VF Corporation internships located?


Four US hubs: Denver, Colorado (Altra, The North Face, JanSport, VF Corporate), Costa Mesa, California (Vans), Stratham, New Hampshire (Timberland), and Greensboro, North Carolina (VF Corporate). Most roles offer relocation and housing stipends.


### Does VF Corporation require a specific GPA for interns?


No. VF publishes no GPA requirement or preference in any of the intern job descriptions reviewed. The focus is on class year (junior or senior at a US four-year university), relevant coursework or degree field, and organizational and communication skills.


### Does VF Corporation sponsor visas for interns?


VF accepts US Citizens, US Permanent Residents, and US Student Visa holders for its summer internship program. This is more inclusive than many large employers that explicitly refuse visa sponsorship. Check individual role postings for the most current requirements.


### What is the VF Corporation intern interview process?


Expect a phone screen with HR followed by a Zoom interview with the hiring manager. Glassdoor rates the process 2.6 out of 5 in difficulty with 100 percent positive experience reported. Average time from application to offer is about 21 days.


### Which VF brands offer internships?


All major VF brands participate. The summer 2026 cohort included interns across The North Face, Vans, Smartwool, icebreaker, Timberland, JanSport, and Altra. Roles span marketing, product development, events, supply chain, finance, and corporate functions.
